source.title: Find Indices With Index and Value Difference II

teaching.hint: For a fixed later index, which earlier indices are eligible, and which values among them are most useful for a large absolute difference?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: For each later index j, eligible partners form a growing prefix. Its minimum and maximum values suffice to test whether any partner differs enough from nums[j].
solution_outline.approach: Scan j in increasing order, extending the eligible prefix through j-indexDifference. Track the indices of its smallest and largest values. Test those two candidate pairs against valueDifference, returning the first valid pair.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before testing j, the tracked minimum and maximum are exactly the extremes among indices at most j-indexDifference. Every tracked index therefore satisfies the distance condition with j.
solution_outline.correctness: Any pair can be ordered with its earlier index first, so a scan over later j loses none. For a fixed j, the largest absolute value difference over its eligible prefix is attained by that prefix's minimum or maximum. If neither qualifies, no eligible partner does; if one qualifies, both conditions hold by construction.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space for n up to 100,000.
solution_outline.pitfall: When indexDifference and valueDifference are zero, pairing an index with itself is valid; excluding equal indices can produce a false no-solution result.

common_wrong_turns: Track only the minimum and miss a large prefix maximum
Require i and j to differ
source_fidelity_notes: Examples were omitted; symmetric absolute conditions, any-answer rule, equal-index allowance, no-solution output, and bounds were retained.
